plain.li: There's the first snow.
Snow already, look at it.
It's sticking, too.
[child] It's snowing, it's snowing!
[child] Can we go out in it?
[child] I'm going to catch one on my tongue.
[lowtech] Bring the wood in before it's buried.
[work:Growing] That's the end of the outdoor fields for this year.
[old] My knees told me this was coming.
[night] Everything's gone quiet with the snow.

warm.li: Look at it coming down, so soft.

cheerful.li: Snow! Who's throwing the first one?

cold.li: We'll be living on the stores from here on.

plain.li: This heat is no joke.
I can hardly breathe out here.
Drink some water, all of you, before you need it.
[work:Growing] The crops are wilting where they stand.
[lowtech] Wet a cloth and keep it on the back of your neck.
[child] It's too hot to play.
[old] I'm too old for heat like this.

warm.li: Come in out of the sun for a bit.

gloomy.li: We're going to bake out here.

cold.li: Work the fields at dawn and dusk until this breaks.

plain.li: My breath's freezing on my scarf.
This cold goes right through you.
[work:Growing] The frost will take the crops if this lasts.
[lowtech] Keep the fires fed tonight.
[!lowtech] Someone check the heaters before dark.
[child] I can't feel my nose.
[old] My bones feel every bit of this cold.

warm.li: Wrap up warm, all of you.

gloomy.li: It's going to be a long, cold night.

cold.li: Double the firewood, and no one goes out alone.

plain.li: Storm's coming in.
Get the washing in before it hits.
[thunder] That one was close.
[thunder] Count the gap between the flash and the bang.
[thunder] Keep away from the tall trees.
[thunder,child] I'm not scared of thunder, I'm not.
[dust] I can't see my own hand in this dust.
[dust] Shut the doors, the dust gets into everything.
[dust] Cover your mouth and nose.
[otherstorm] Look at the sky, it's gone strange.

gloomy.li: Something's going to get hit tonight.

cold.li: Tie down anything loose before it arrives.

plain.li: First snow today. The yard went white in an hour, and by evening the footprints had frozen hard.
Snow came in during the night. Everything sounds softer this morning.
The first snow of the winter. I stood out in it longer than I needed to.
[child] It snowed! I made a snow angel, got cold, and made another one.
[child] Snow today. I tried to catch every flake on my tongue and lost count.
[lowtech] First snow. We carried wood until dark and stacked it against the north wall.
[work:Growing] Snow on the fields this morning. Whatever is still out there won't last the week.
[old] Another winter starting. I've seen enough of them to know this one will be long.

warm.li: The first snow, and someone had the kettle on before I was even up.

blunt.li: Snow. Cleared the paths twice today.

cheerful.li: Snow! We had a snowball fight before breakfast and I won, more or less.

gloomy.li: Snow again. The days are getting shorter and the stores aren't getting fuller.

cold.li: First snowfall. Noted the date, checked the stores against the days until spring.

plain.li: The heat won't break. We drank more water today than we cooked with.
Too hot to sleep. I lay on the floor where the stone was coolest.
[work:Growing] The leaves are curling in the fields. I watered twice and it wasn't enough.
[lowtech] Kept a wet cloth on the back of my neck all day, and wet it again every hour.
[child] It's so hot. We were allowed to splash water at each other.

gloomy.li: Another day of this heat. Even the flies have stopped moving.

plain.li: The cold came down overnight. The water bucket by the door froze solid.
Slept in every layer I own and still woke up shivering.
[lowtech] We kept the fires going all night, taking turns.
[work:Growing] Frost on everything this morning. I'm afraid to look at the fields.
[child] It was so cold my eyelashes had frost on them.

warm.li: Bitter cold, so we all crowded into the warmest room and told stories until late.

gloomy.li: The cold won't let up. I can't remember what it felt like to be warm.

plain.li: A storm today. We tied down what we could and waited it out.
[thunder] Thunder all night. I counted the seconds after each flash, like I was taught as a child.
[thunder] Lightning struck somewhere close. The whole room went white.
[dust] A dust storm today. There's grit in my teeth, my bed and my food.
[otherstorm] The sky went a color I've never seen before. We all stayed in.
[child] There was a big storm. I hid under the blanket, but only for a bit.

gloomy.li: Storm all day. Felt like the sky had a grudge against us.

plain.li: I've never known it this cold here.
Coldest night since we came, I'd swear to it.
Even the stones are cracking in this cold.
[old] My bones don't remember a cold like this one.
[child] It's colder than it's ever been!

gloomy.li: Every winter here finds a new way to be worse.

plain.li: It's never been this hot here, not since we came.
The air shakes over the ground today.
[work:Growing] The fields have never had a day like this.
[old] I've lived through some summers, and none was this hot.
[child] The ground's too hot to walk on!
Has it ever rained this long here?
Another day of rain, and I've stopped counting them.
[work:Growing] The roots will rot if this keeps on.
[child] Is it ever going to stop raining?

cheerful.li: The wells will be full for a year after this.

plain.li: Not a drop in days, longer than I've ever seen here.
The dust gets into everything when it's this dry.
[work:Growing] The fields are cracking for want of rain.
[child] When is it going to rain again?

gloomy.li: The sky has forgotten how to rain.

plain.li: [colder] This {SEASON} was colder than the last one. We burned through the wood faster than I counted on.
[colder,winter] A harder winter than last year's. I wrote down every morning the water froze in the bucket, and the list is long.
[warmer] This {SEASON} was warmer than last year's. The flies stayed longer and so did the light.
[warmer,winter] A mild winter, milder than the one before. The ground barely froze.
[wetter] More rain this {SEASON} than last year, and the paths show it.
[wetter,spring] A wet spring, wetter than the last. The seed beds had to be dug twice.
[drier] A drier {SEASON} than last year's. I watched the sky more than I watched the work.
[drier,summer] Hardly any rain this summer, much less than last year's. The well rope reaches further every week.
[stormier] Storm after storm this {SEASON}, far more than the year before.

gloomy.li: [stormier] The storms this {SEASON} never seemed to end. Last year we didn't know how lucky we were.

plain.li: The sky's gone green; that's hail coming.
Get the ripe rows in, there's hail in that sky.
Smell that, and look at the color of it: hail.
[work:Growing] Leave the weeding and cut what's ripe, hail's coming.
[old] I've seen that green before, and hail always followed it.
[lowtech] The birds have gone quiet, so hail's on its way.

gloomy.li: There goes half the harvest, unless we're quick.

plain.li: The wind's turned, feel how warm it is.
Warm air from the south, and out of season too.
[work:Growing] A few more growing days, if this holds.
[child] It's warm enough to go without a coat!

cheerful.li: Now that's a gift of a day.

gloomy.li: It won't last, it never does.

plain.li: That one was close.
Count, just count, it's further than it looks.
I hate this, I hate every flash of it.
[child] I'm not scared, I'm just standing here.

gloomy.li: Who is it for this time?

plain.li: Good thing we put that rod up.
Straight into the rod, just like it should.
[child] The lightning hit the pole, did you see?

cheerful.li: Missed us, you big flash, try again!

plain.li: A tornado went across the land today. We watched it from the doorways, a grey rope from the sky to the ground, until it broke up.
The wind tore across the fields this afternoon in a twisting column. Afterwards there was a path through the grass as if a giant had walked it.
[child] There was a tornado! It looked like a big grey snake. I wasn't scared, I was inside.

gloomy.li: A tornado came through. It took what it wanted and left. That's the way of things here.
